title: GST Accounting with Sage UBS
description: Learn how to use the latest Sage UBS accounting software with GST support.

asr.full_text: Hello, welcome to GST Accounting course using Sage UBS 2015. To begin, in lesson 1, we learn about the setup and settings. Throughout this lesson, you will understand how to enable GST features and functionalities. Within the application and how to maintain key data elements for GST reporting. In the Accounting Application module, go to the Country setting, set the country as Malaysia,. Then click on the Advanced setting. After that, select and check the options of With Purchase Tax, With Sales Tax, and With. GST. At the Inventory and Billing Application module, go to the Country setting, set the country. As Malaysia as well. Now let's look into the general setup in the Accounting Application module. If your company is a GST registered company, enter the Major Industry Code and select With. Malaysia GST option. After you have selected the With Malaysia GST option, the GST Settings tab will be enabled. Enter your GST Registration Number, GST Taxable Period, GST Effective Date and GST Filing Date. This information will be printed on your GST-03 form. The GST Effective Date is very important. It will tell the system when to enable the GST features. Let's say you set the GST effective date as 1st of April 2015. On the 1st of April 2015, when you first log in to the system, a message will be shown. To inform you that the GST feature is now enabled in the system. Lastly, make sure you map the appropriate GL account to each setting. In the General Setup of Inventory and Billing Application module, go to the Company Profile. To make sure you fill in your Company Name, Company Address, Company Registration Number. And GST Registration Number. All the information will be printed on your invoice header, therefore ensure that it is. Correct and accurate. Make sure you select the With Malaysia GST option. Malaysia GST features will be enabled immediately after you save this setting. Next, go to the Transaction tab. You will notice that the options with per item tax, with per item discount are checked and it is not allowed to change. The reason is, in the GST audit file, the taxable amount shown for each item line must be after the discount amount and the tax amount for each item line must be shown individually. There are 6 important master data that you need to take note. First, the GL accounts. For all GL accounts related to GST, please set special account equal to PT for input tax related and ST for output tax related. The 7 GL accounts here are customs recommended GL accounts. GST input tax for acquisition, GST output tax for supply, GST control account to show net tax effect payable or claimable,. GST liability for GST bad debt handling on customer, GST claimable for GST bad debt handling on supplier,. GST suspense for GST on importation of goods and GST expense for no claimable input tax. Secondly, let us look at the GST tax codes. All customs recommended tax codes are provided in. The system, thus you do not need to create it by yourself. For certain tax code such as BL,. Which is the block input text. You are encouraged to map it to GST Expenses GL account. So that it will be reflected correctly in your profit and loss report. Third, the customer maintenance at the master data. It is important to ensure all information. Related to GST are filled into the customer maintenance as it is needed for GST audit file. Purpose. At number four, we need to maintain the master data for the suppliers. It is important. To ensure all information related to GST are filled into the supplier maintenance as it is. Also needed for GST audit file purpose. Please take note that RMCD approval code is meant for. Supplier whom you will issue invoice on behalf of the supplier. Let's take an example, the. Klaper Sawit plantation farmers due to situation where they may not know the market price of the. Klaper Sawit, so the cooking oil production company who is their customer will issue invoices. On behalf of the farmers. Fifth in the setup is the item group setup. You can set the default. Purchase tax code and default sales tax code for each item group. We encourage you to categorize. Your items by type of supply and link them to the respective item group so that in the future. If there is any change of the GST text code. You just need to change it in the item group. Instead of amending it in each item. During transaction entry, if an item is linked to an. Item group, the respective default GST text code will be shown automatically. As for the sixth setup, we need to ensure the following is maintained at the item. You can also. Map the default purchase tax code and supplier. Tax code to each item so that during transaction entry. The GST tax code will be shown automatically. Now at this point we have. Completed lesson 1. In this lesson you have. Learned the steps to enable GST features and fill. Up GST registration details, maintain key data. Elements in master data for GST reporting. We shall now move to lesson 2, how do you. Import the transactions. In this lesson, you will learn 3 important key areas. 1. How do you enter GST related purchasing entries? 2. How do you enter GST-related sales entries? 3. How do you post the transactions to accounting? Let us start with the purchase transaction entries. The supplier invoices, purchase credit notes, purchase debit notes, and self-billed invoices will be entered via inventory and billing system. After that, you will post the transactions to accounting. When you make payment to your supplier, you will enter the payment transaction via accounting system and offset with the invoices, credit notes and debit notes. Let us look into some important areas related to GST. They are received and received by self-billed invoice. Invoice not paid within 6 months and payment for outstanding invoices that are more than 6 months. Import of service and also capital goods handling. When you receive a supplier invoice from your supplier, you will create a receive transaction. After you have selected the item, the related GST tax code will be shown. And the GST amount is calculated automatically as well. Once the supplier invoice is posted, editing will not be allowed. If you need to issue a self-built invoice on behalf of your supplier,. Firstly, make sure the supplier is a GST registered company. Secondly, make sure it is approved by customs and an approval code is given. Maintain the approval code in the supplier file maintenance. To enter a self-billed invoice, go to the Transactions menu and click on Receive Self-Build Menu. After you have entered and saved the self-billed invoice, you will need to print a copy of the invoice and send to your supplier. In the GST regulations, outstanding supplier invoices which are more than 6 months must, I repeat again,. Must have the claimed GST input tax be refunded back to customs. To cater for this type, go to Transactions menu, click on GST Bad Debt Journal, AP, and then select Refund Customs. Select the supplier and all the outstanding invoices for more than 6 months will be listed automatically. Select the invoices, which you need to refund the input tax claim to customs, and the financial entries will be generated automatically. These financial entries are generated based on the GL accounts mapped in the housekeeping menu. Run Setup, General Setup at the GST setting. Click Save to save the transaction. When you have paid to your supplier for those outstanding invoices where the output tax adjustment has been processed, you may now claim those GST back from customs again. To keep this record, go to Transactions menu, GST Back That Journal for AP, click on Reclaim Customs. Select the supplier and only outstanding invoices of the selected supplier where output tax adjustment has been processed for tax refund from customs will be listed. Select the invoices which you need to claim back the input tax refunded from customs and the financial entries will be generated automatically. These financial entries are generated based on the GL Accounts map in the Housekeeping menu, Run Setup, General Setup, GST Setting. Click Save to save the transactions. All imported services acquired for the purpose of business except exempt supply of services will be subjected to GST. The GST on imported services is payable by the recipient of the services using the reverse charge mechanism. An item with service type must first be created in a system via maintenance menu, item maintenance, then at the item file maintenance. To record this type of transaction, go to transaction menu, click on receive. Remember to click Import Service checkbox on the header to indicate that this is an importation of service. After you have entered the payment transaction, go to Transactions menu, Open Item menu, Creditor,. Then select Knock-off Bills to offset the invoice and the payment. GST on imported services is only accounted for at the point when the transactions are being offset. Reverse mechanism treatment for input tax TX and output tax DS is automated in the system to ease your transaction worries. The definition of capital goods under GST context are as the following. 1. It is capitalized under accepted accounting principles. 2. It is used in the course of furtherance of a business. 3. That it is not for the purpose of reselling. Lastly, each unit valued at RM100,000 or more and exclusive of GST. To record this type of transaction, go to Periodic menu, Capital Goods and select Maintain Capital Goods to maintain the capital goods details after you have purchased it. If your company is making wholly taxable supply only, then you can claim the input tax for the capital goods purchased in full in the period you purchased it. If your company is making both taxable and exempted supply, then you will need to make annual adjustments to the input tax claim. For equipment, machinery, vehicles, it is at 5 intervals. For land, building, it is at 10 intervals. When the transaction is saved, the intervals will be populated according on the type selected starting from the year of purchase. Next, let us discuss about sales transaction entries. The sales invoices, sales credit notes, sales debit notes and cash sales will be entered via inventory and billing system. After that, you will post the transactions to accounting. When you receive payment from your customer. You will enter the received transaction via accounting module. And offset with the invoices, credit notes and debit notes. Here, we shall see the important GST-related areas in sales. There are the tax invoice, credit note and debit note. With or without reason description. Prepayment is an important aspect too. We will learn about bad debt relief and also the bad debt recovered. When you want to issue an invoice to your customer, you will create an invoice. After you have selected the item, the related GST tax code will be shown and the GST amount is calculated automatically as well. You can print a tax invoice from the system. Once the invoice is posted, editing will not be allowed. According to Goods and Services Tax Act 2014,. If there are changes in quantity, amount, tax rate or cancellation of transactions,. Credit note or debit note must be issued by the related parties. When you create a credit note or debit note, remember to select the Update from Invoice option so that system will prompt the list of the invoices. Click the Accept button and the Select Invoice screen will be prompted. Select the Related Sales Invoice, all information from the invoice will be copied to the debit note. In the body section, select the reason of issuing the credit note. The reason is maintainable at Maintenance menu, Miscellaneous Files. Click on the reason maintenance. In the credit note and debit note printout, you will see that the related invoice number,. Invoice date and the reason is printed on it. When you receive prepayment or advance payment from your customer and it will be used as part payment for the supply that you are going to make, you need to account GST for the prepayment or advance payment. The prepayment or advance payment will be considered as inclusive of GST. When you enter the receipt transaction, select the prepayment option. Once the receipt entry is saved, financial entries will be generated with GST inclusive. In the GST regulation, the paid GST output tax for those outstanding sales invoices which are more than 6 months can be claimed back from customs. Go to the Transactions menu, select GST Bad Debt Journal AR, then click on Bad Debt Relief. Select the customer. All outstanding invoices of the selected customer that have exceeded 6 months, as on the date set in Journal Date Field, will be listed. Take on the checkboxes to mark the invoices to process. The financial entries will be generated automatically by the system with tax code to ease your journal entry transactions. They are strictly for viewing and not editable. These financial entries are generated based on the GL accounts mapped in the housekeeping menu,. Run Setup, General Setup, GST Settings. Click Save to save the transactions. When your customer has settled the outstanding invoices, you will need to refund the output tax claim to customs. Select the customer and only outstanding invoices of the selected customer where bad debt relief had been processed for GST refund will be listed in this section. Take on the checkboxes to mark the invoices to process the tax refund to customs. The financial entries will be generated automatically by the system with tax code to ease your journal entries. They are strictly for viewing and not editable. These financial entries are generated based on the GL accounts mapped in the housekeeping menu, Run Setup, General Setup, GST Setting. Click Save to save the transaction. Transactions from inventory and billing system must be posted to accounting system. Only posted transactions will be taken for GST reporting. This is to comply with GST Act where confirmed and posted transactions cannot be edited and will remain unchanged to support the values reported and submitted to customs in a case of an audit call. Changes, if required, will be carried out via appropriate adjustment documents like credit note or debit note. All posted bills need to be imported into accounting system for generation of GAF purposes. We have now completed Lesson 2. In this lesson, you have learned about the important GSD areas in purchase entries,. Important GST areas in sales entries. And the importance of posting and export import of bills. In Lesson 3, we will cover the required reports for GST implementation. In this lesson, you will understand about the important documents and reports related to GST. The highlighted are the required fields for a valid tax invoice, credit notes and debit notes. Any of these fields not shown in the source document will be considered as invalid GST source documents. Issuing an invalid GST source document is considered as fraud and will lead to penalty and jail imprisonment. There is also Print Control implemented for printing of source documents. When you print the source document again, the word Duplicate Copy will be printed. For self-built invoice, make sure the approval number is printed on it. The system provides a wizard-driven guide on generating the output similar to that of. GST03 form that is to facilitate users in processing the periodic GST return. The GST return function is located at Reports menu, Goods and Services text,. Malaysia GST, then click on GST return visit. Just go through each step and. Check the amount being generated. All the amount shown on screen are not editable. At the end of the process, if you submit the report as final, the print button becomes available for you to print out a mock-up of a GST03 for reference. You may use it as a reference guide when processing actual GST return on the authority's website. You can also generate the tab file for online submission. If you save the report as draft, you will not be able to print the GST03 form and also. Not able to generate the tax file. The Goods and Services Tax Report is meant to assist you in reconciling the amount shown. In the GST return with the list of detailed transactions. All the transactions presented in this report are grouped by respective GST tax codes. GST audit file is one of the mandatory reports that is required under the GST ruling and need to be produced and submitted upon request from JKDM when they conduct periodic audits to ensure tax returns are being prepared correctly. The GAF is a file containing standard set of accounting information found in General Ledger together with detailed breakdown of business transactions found in details of invoices, orders and adjustments for audit purpose. You can generate either the text format or XML format from the system. We have come to the end of GST accounting course using SISH UBS 2015. In this lesson, you have learned about the mandatory fields in a valid GST source documents,. Print control and generate all GST related reports such as the goods and service tax report, GST return and GST audit file. Thank you for attending and have fun with your Sage UBS 2015.
